scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The dance originated with the Minangkabau people of West Sumatra during the era of Indonesian kingdoms.
It is traditionally linked to a folk tale about a girl searching for her lost engagement ring with a candle on a plate, whose frantic yet careful movements became the basis for the choreography.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Originally a harvest ritual to thank God and the community's deity for prosperity, it now serves as entertainment.
It is commonly performed at weddings after the pasambahan ceremony and at public cultural events.
Today it is a living tradition.
on_screen: Footage — MISSING (use images)

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: Dancers hold small plates with burning candles in their palms.
The primary technique involves rotating the plates on a horizontal plane while the body bends, twists, and turns.
It is performed in groups, often by women or in male-female pairs, requiring significant balance to keep the candles lit.
Watch for Plate Rotation.

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The dance is accompanied by traditional Minang music.
Key instruments include the Talempong (gongs), Saluang (flute), and Kendang (drums), which create a rhythmic and melodic backdrop for the dancers' movements.
Listen for the Talempong, Saluang, Kendang.
The sound is dominated by the metallic, melodic chiming of the Talempong gongs, supported by the rhythmic pulse of the Kendang drums and the melodic, breathy lines of the Saluang bamboo flute.

scenes.title: The people
narration: While originating in West Sumatra, the dance has spread across Indonesia and is also recognized as a subclass of Malaysian dance traditions.
The dance is a traditional Minangkabau folk dance and shares technical similarities with the Tari Piring (Plate Dance) and the Pandanggo of the Philippines.

scenes.title: Family tree
narration: Lilin dance is sibling of Tari Piring: Both involve balancing plates on the palms, though Tari Piring uses plates without candles and often involves clinking them with rings.
Lilin dance is variant of Pandanggo: A Philippine dance that also involves balancing candles (often in glasses) on the head and hands.
